item.title: Not much relief in sight for Prairie drought
item.description: There is not much relief in sight for the drought in western Saskatchewan and central and southern Alberta.

item.title: In defence of eating oats
item.description: Forget any social media fear mongering about oats — Oats are a healthy, nutritious, Prairie-grown option to add more whole grains to your diet.

item.title: Fertilizer industry optimistic about red tape reduction
item.description: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency had a rule requiring labels on all fertilizer sold in Canada, but the agency is now working with industry to change that regulation.

item.title: U.S. urges WTO members to rethink core tariff rule in face of China threat
item.description: The Trump administration on Monday urged World Trade Organization members to rethink the body’s core principle of “Most Favored Nation” bound tariff rates, arguing in a new position paper that this has led to discriminatory practices and imbalanced trade, including with China.

item.title: Sun’s movement drives our weather
item.description: In this article we are back to looking at day length, the “march of the seasons” as it is often called, and atmospheric composition.

item.title: FCC raises inflation forecast on surging commodity prices
item.description: Farm Credit Canada has raised its 2026 forecast for overall inflation as commodity prices spike due to war in the Middle East.

item.title: Farmland climbs higher in spite of headwinds
item.description: In a year with trade disruptions, higher input costs and economic uncertainty, agricultural land in Canada continued to climb higher in value

item.title: University of Saskatchewan crop breeder recognized internationally
item.description: Curtis Pozniak, Curtis Pozniak, director of the University of Saskatchewan’s Crop Development Centre, recently received the Bertebos Prize, recognizing the impact of research in the agricultural food supply.
